Unrefereed six-week-old preprint with internally inconsistent AI attribution; object description only from secondary summaries. In any case it concerns the stable forking conjecture, not stable fields.
events.ai_basis: This is an AI-generated result proven with the help of GPT-5.6 Sol.

why: Every result on the statement itself predates the snapshot and restricts it to a class (omega-stable, superstable, bounded, weight 1, finite dp-rank, large), so each is a case; the journal-published ones count as digested by journals of record. Scanlon's note proves a weaker property (Artin-Schreier closure), not separable closure, for any class, so it settles no restriction: none. Duret's result is a reduction to the open simple fields conjecture: none, with an unplaceable date. In the window: Kaplan-Matthews-Walsberg only re-prove the known large-field case (none), the Johnson talk states a conjecture (none), and Bartnick assumes stability (none). Freitag-Mutchnik is about the stable forking conjecture, a different problem that shares a word, so it is a variant. Its own quotes say the counterexample was AI-generated, so it is coded generated for that event alone, and it contributes nothing to this problem.
doubts: Freitag-Mutchnik's AI role is stated inconsistently in the paper (it also says the proofs were written entirely by the authors). Reading it as generated rather than assisted has no effect here because the event is a variant. The Poizat bounded case rests on unverified secondary sources.
